name: Tremere's Inner Circle (Libellus Sanguinis II Lore)

pages.name: Tremere and the Sleep of Ceoris

text.content: In 1022, the Hermetic magus @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere} led seven fellow magi in a ritual meant to grant true immortality; it instead damned them as vampires by stealing the blood and dominion of the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.nyOuQ8xvZEiNEJbM]{Tzimisce} Antediluvian Saulot. Shortly after returning from Saulot's haven bearing the power of the Third Generation, @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere} gathered his closest advisors — Etrius, Goratrix, and Meerlinda among them — and declared simply, "It is done. We are a clan by blood and by destiny," before voluntarily entering torpor for the good of his new clan and the repose of his own soul. He has not been seen since; some Tremere who witnessed his return describe his bearing as exultant yet strangely guarded, as if the act had sparked an inner war he never resolved. Decades later, the fortress of Ceoris itself is said to groan under the weight of something vast and restless stirring in its depths, and rumors persist among the clan's scholars that Tremere's sacrifice weighs on him rather more than Saulot's death ever could.

One of the original seven magi transformed alongside @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere}, Etrius now serves as the ceaseless guardian of his slumbering founder, watching over Ceoris and, at times, Vienna. Where his fellow elder Goratrix revels in the clan's new nature, Etrius has never made peace with the price of immortality; a century after the transformation his letters still dwell on the horror of what House @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere} became and his enduring anger at Goratrix for engineering the change in the first place. His reluctance and melancholy have become something of a running joke among younger Tremere, even as his authority within the Inner Council remains unquestioned.

The architect of Clan @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere}'s transformation from mortal magi to immortal Cainites, Goratrix now leads the clan's expansion into France from his labyrinthine Paris chantry, protected by Gargoyle servitors of his own creation. Utterly unrepentant about the cost of the clan's founding, he considers Etrius's continued guilt tiresome and beneath a being who has "attained transformation beyond our most potent imaginings." His ongoing alchemical experiments on human and Cainite subjects — whom he refers to, with obvious relish, as his "toys" — have advanced the clan's occult knowledge considerably, at a moral cost few other @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere} are willing to discuss openly.

A young ghoul apprentice bound to Meerlinda's service at her Durham chantry, Geraint de Montfort represents a typical @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere} Embrace of the era: a mortal wizard of promise, carefully schooled for years before being drained and reborn through the same ritual that transformed the clan's founders. Rescued from religious searches for the Grail and Sangreal by the more immediate promise of immortality at his sire's hand, Geraint's transformation and oath of loyalty to Meerlinda and the wider pyramid stand as a model of how the clan continues to recruit and indoctrinate new blood a century after @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere}'s own transformation.

vtmlarp.source: Libellus Sanguinis II: Keepers of the Word, Book Two: Usurpers
